acceptance: 1) Entry: Sign out all devices (devices-signout-all) on /admin/account/devices -> shared confirmation -> POST /api/admin/account/reauth(purpose=LOGOUT_ALL) -> POST /api/admin/account/logout-all. Data source: GET devices. In two real browsers both old cookies get 401 from GET account and return to login (E-03). 2) Expired/wrong-purpose grants cause no sign-out. A timeout replays neither the grant nor trigger. Verify with safe GET; if signed out, verify through ordinary login. Ordinary single-device signOut still requires no current password (E-73, E-74). Use the unique minimalist-flat style from section 11. At the actual service at 1920x1080, 1440x900, and 390x844, record GIFs and computed styles: 2px black borders, zero radius, no shadow, and accent #b45700. On each admin page, run D1-D6 and overflow probes with work/form/card and density7/gutter16/gap16/pad16. Labels and keyboard focus are reachable; touch-control targets measure at least 44px. 3) Directly assert the control/protocol sequence. Clicking devices-signout-all opens confirmation describing all-device impact. Cancel sends zero POST reauth/logout-all requests and both browsers still get 200 from GET /api/admin/account. Confirming and completing shared identity verification sends exactly one POST /api/admin/account/reauth with body={purpose:LOGOUT_ALL,password,totp}; after its 200 token response, send exactly one POST /api/admin/account/logout-all with body={actionGrant:token}. Sign-out returns 2xx and validates against the M1-T2 SignedOutDTO schema. Set-Cookie expires the same-named Auth.js authentication cookie used at initial sign-in. Both browsers then get 401 from GET /api/admin/account; current pathname is /admin-login and the device table is no longer displayed. Calling logout-all with a grant at the five-minute deadline or wrong purpose returns 401/error=action_grant_invalid; both browsers still get 200 from GET account and the dialog requests fresh verification. Test two unknown-outcome cases: lose the response after service commit, then safe GET account=401 leads to login; interrupt before sending, then safe GET account=200 keeps the devices page and displays confirmation-unknown. Observe each for 15 seconds without a second reauth/logout-all. Clicking ordinary current-device signOut sends no reauth; it follows the original Auth.js sign-out protocol and its old cookie gets 401 from GET account.

E-03.trigger: The password is changed, the authenticator is reset, the account is disabled, or Sign out all devices is executed.
E-03.expect: Revoke the account's old credentials on the server; reject old JWTs even if they have not expired. Ordinary Sign out must at least revoke the current device session and clear the local signed-in state.

E-73.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-73.trigger: Two requests use the same ActionGrant concurrently, or a password-change grant is used to disable the authenticator.
E-73.expect: Within the sensitive-change transaction, validate and consume the grant once against the action, device, account, and credential version. Only one matching request succeeds; reject a mismatched purpose without executing the change.

E-74.scene: Fresh identity verification for sensitive settings
E-74.trigger: More than five minutes have elapsed since grant issuance, the device is revoked, the password/authenticator changes, or the account's permission becomes invalid.
E-74.expect: The old grant immediately becomes invalid. Fresh-verification grants cannot be transferred between devices and cannot extend the original device-session lifetime.
